Job Description
About Council
Moorabool Shire Council is a progressive organisation that is experiencing rapid growth and surging development. We offer a perfect blend of picturesque and friendly surrounds where you can enjoy an urban lifestyle in towns like Bacchus Marsh or take advantage of Moorabool’s smaller towns and hamlets, rural open spaces and natural surrounds.
Our focus is on building a healthy, inclusive and connected community; a liveable and thriving environment and an organisation that listens and adapts to the need of our evolving communities.
The Role
As the Asset Systems Officer, you will play a key role in supporting the effective management of Council's infrastructure assets through the administration, maintenance and continuous improvement of Council's asset and maintenance management systems. Reporting to the Coordinator Asset Management, you will ensure the quality, integrity and usability of asset data, coordinate infrastructure inspection programs, develop reporting and analysis tools, and support the integration of asset information across multiple systems. Working closely with internal stakeholders, contractors and service providers, you will contribute to informed decision-making, improved service delivery and the sustainable management of assets across our growing municipality.
Click here to view the position description or click the link in 'how to apply'
If you have questions specific to the role, please contact Natalie Coakley (Coordinator Asset Management) on 03 5366 1346
What We Offer
Outstanding flexible working arrangements - make working with us work for you
Monthly RDO
Up to two additional annual leave days depending on leave accruals
Access to 3 health and wellbeing days over the life of our Health and Wellbeing Strategy
Eligibility for parental leave after six months service
Employee Assistance Program
Flexibility Spread of Hours Clause
Updates to our Discretionary Leave Clause to include gender affirmation related activities, natural disaster and foster caring
Send us an email at peopleservices@moorabool.vic.gov.au and we can chat about all the benefits of working at Moorabool. We’d love to chat with you about our culture, development frameworks, progression opportunities, cultural initiatives, reward frameworks and flexibility opportunities.
About You
You are an organised and solutions-focused professional with experience in asset, maintenance or information management systems. You bring strong data analysis and problem-solving skills, a passion for continuous improvement, and the ability to translate technical information into practical outcomes. With excellent communication skills and a collaborative approach, you can support users, improve system performance, and ensure the integrity of critical asset information. If you're motivated by using data and technology to support smarter asset management and better community outcomes, we'd love to hear from you.
How To Apply
Please visit our website to apply online @ https//www.moorabool.vic.gov.au/vacancies
When you hit the apply button you won’t be required to complete lengthy key selection criteria, instead you will be asked to pitch to Council as to why you are the best candidate for this role.
You’ll also be asked to tell us what interview style works best for you. We want to make sure your interview experience is one that you feel comfortable with and that you leave your interview knowing the best version of yourself was on offer.
Applications will close by 11.59pm on Thursday 8 October 2026.
If you are experiencing difficulties with your application please contact Lisa Grey People Services Lead on 5366 1272.
Moorabool Shire Council is proudly committed to:
Being a family friendly, gender inclusive and equal opportunity employer
Promoting the safety, wellbeing and inclusion of all children under the age of 18
Supporting the Human Rights Charter
**Please be advised we do not accept applications through agencies**
We encourage applications from Aboriginal people, people from culturally and/or linguistically diverse backgrounds and people with a disability
Only those with the right to work in Australia will be considered.

POSITION DESCRIPTION
Asset Systems Officer
Position number                  AST011
Directorate                      Community Assets & Infrastructure
Service unit                     Asset Management
Classification                   Band (6) (Moorabool Shire Council Enterprise Agreement No 10, 2023)
Reports to                Coordinator Asset Management
Organisational                   Directly supervises       Asset Inspections Officer & Asset Data Officer
relationships                                              Staff at all levels of the organisation, service
Internal relationships
providers, and contractors
Residents, customers, service authorities,
External relationships
contractors, subcontractors and suppliers
Probation period                 6 months (applies to all new employees)
Approved by (position title)     GM Community Assets and Infrastructure
Date                             June 2024
To provide high quality customer focused support service to users in
the implementation and development of Council’s Maintenance
Management and Asset Management Systems and coordinate inspection
Position purpose                 services for all Infrastructure Assets.
•   To coordinate accurate and efficient proactive inspections of all
infrastructure assets in line with Council’s Road Management Plan.
•   To implement, develop and operate Council’s Asset Management
and Maintenance Management Systems for all infrastructure assets
including but not limited to roads, drainage, kerb, bridges, parks and
associated infrastructure.
.
Key responsibilities and duties
Systems Management
•   Develop and implement Council's Asset Management System (AMS) and Maintenance Management
Systems (MMS) including customised reporting and the development of templates.
•   Validate and maintain data within the systems ensuring it is up to date and accurate.
•   Support the implementation and maintenance of Council’s AMS and MMS, integration, databases and
registers for data quality control ensuring consistency, integrity and accuracy of all asset inventory,
condition and valuation information.
•   Support the development and review of asset management policies, plans, strategies, systems and
processes that ensure asset management objectives are met, and ensure they are up to date and
communicated across the organisation as appropriate.
•   Using asset systems, develop financial and statistical reporting and assist in the development of capital
renewal programs.
•   Provide support and assistance to relevant teams in the development of programmed maintenance
inspections and activities within the MMS.
•   Provide support and assistance to the relevant teams in the ongoing use of the AMS and MMS.
•   Ensure that the inspection regimes and intervention levels in the MMS are in accordance with relevant
maintenance management plans.
•   Coordinate proactive inspections for all asset classes and ensure that all inspection data is documented in
the MMS and required maintenance and identified defects are allocated to the appropriate service unit.
•   Assist the coordinator in arranging periodic asset condition inspections on all asset classes updating
relevant systems accordingly.
•   Train new staff and provide refresher training on the MMS and AMS as required, including the use of field
based electronic systems.
•   Liaise with the AMS, MMS, and associated systems software providers on issues relating to software
operation and development.
•   Work at continuous improvement by documentation of processes and procedures for the assets unit as
required.
•   Facilitate and manage one off project outcomes as required.
•   Adhere to all Council’s policies and procedures as relevant to this position.
•   Assist in meeting corporate objectives and sectional requirements by carrying out other duties as deemed
reasonable and appropriate to the role as directed from time to time.
Staff Supervision
•   Monitor, document and report quality, OHS, environmental performance within areas of responsibility,
including undertaking field spot checks as required.
•   Supervise staff as required, ensuring that work is carried out in accordance with legislative and Council
requirements.
•   Monitor staff attendance and start/finish times and verify timesheets.
•   In conjunction with the Asset Management Coordinator, undertake annual reviews of staff that the
position supervises in accordance with timelines and procedures.
Contract Supervision
•   Assist in the development of specifications, procurement, evaluation, appointment and management of
contractors.
•   Undertake supervision and surveillance of contractors, ensuring that work is carried out in accordance
with legislative and specified requirements.
•   Assess and verify works carried out against contractor payment claims and budget, and process payments.
•   Provide reports on the progress of contracts and variations including preparation of reports on, and
evaluation of, contractor performance.
•   Order contractors, goods, materials and services in accordance with procurement policy, prepare, check
and process (within approval limits) the necessary documentation.
Customer Service
•   Provide high level customer service ensuring that all enquiries are dealt with promptly and courteously
and that the response is in accordance with Council’s customer service standards.
•   Monitor the status of the customer request system and phone requests relevant to the position and
report to supervisors as required.
Occupational Health & Safety
•   Maintain and foster a safe work environment at all times.
•   Follow safe work practices, procedures, instructions and rules at all times.
•   Perform all duties in a manner that ensure personal health and safety, and that of others in the workplace
and the general public.
•   Regularly inspect own immediate work environment and report all hazards or incidents that can cause
harm or that represent a threat to public safety.
All Councillors, employees, consultants, volunteers, work experience students and contractors are to work
within the constraints by the provisions of the Occupational.
Health Safety Act 2004 and the Occupational Health and Safety Regulations 2007 and any other applicable
legislation relevant to their duties or tasks. Further, they will also work under the conditions set out in any
relevant Moorabool Shire Policy or Procedure to ensure safety.
Specific responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
•   Actively participate in on the job training as required.
•   Share a responsibility for OHS, both for themselves and for others working with them.
•   Report immediately any injury or near miss encountered during the duties or undertaking Council
activities.
•   Immediately take appropriate action to remove (if appropriate) or control any hazard observed.
•   Use appropriate personal protective equipment provided by the Council.
•   Create Safe Operating Procedures for operations relevant to the position and ensure they are
documented accordingly and complied with and signed off in the field.
Risk Management
Council, Management, employees, work experience students, volunteers and contractors all have joint
responsibility of making risk management a priority as they undertake tasks in delivering Council’s services
and achieving Council’s objectives.
Specific responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
•   Provide support to management to systematically identify, assess and manage risks and opportunities in
their functional area, including the development and implementation of approved work practices
•   Ensure that policy is communicated to employees, work experience students, volunteers and contractors.
•   Consult with employees, volunteers and contractors to identify, assess and manage risks and opportunities
associated with their work.
•   Implement Risk Management policies and procedures to meet legislative requirements.
•   Ensure Council’s Risk Management policy and Risk Management practices within the workplace and the
community are observed and complied with at all times.
•   Ensure the implementation of hazard and environmental aspect inspections, risk assessments and risk
controls.
•   Review, investigate and report all incidents.
•   Initiate actions to continuously improve the Risk Management System.
Accountability and Extent of Authority
•   Accountable for creating and capturing accurate and complete records of the business activities related
to this position, in accordance with approved policy and procedures. This is applicable to both hardcopy
and electronic information, including email.
•   The incumbent can give direction to team members, provided that these directions/instructions are within
the incumbent’s skill/training and level of authority or involves the explanation of established procedures
and practices.
•   Ensuring the maintenance programs and database are up to date and complies with operational plan
requirements.
•   Providing high level, courteous and efficient customer service.
•   Maintaining security and confidentiality of all documentation.
•   Providing accurate information as requested.
•   Ensuring that the standard of work performed meets the requirements of the organisation and service
unit standards and the responsibilities of the position.
•   Ability to work both unsupervised and as part of a team.
Judgement and Decision Making
•   Use initiative appropriately in handling activities or projects on behalf of the Asset Management
Coordinator.
•   Respond to all requests for service and carry out duties according to policy, procedure and standards
established within the section, requiring some personal judgement.
•   Providing advice and support to users with the implementation and development of the AMS and MMS.
•   Guidance will always be available and will be provided by the Asset Management Coordinator and
management.

...
Qualifications, skills and experience
Qualifications
•     Tertiary qualification (or working towards completing) or significant relevant experience in information
technology, asset and maintenance management or database management.
Skills and experience
•     High-level customer services focus with excellent communication skills (oral and written) and an ability to
work at the team member level.
•     Demonstrated experience in the use of AMS and MMS.
•     Proven ability to operate computer-based programs such as those with the Microsoft Office suite of
programs and experience administering databases, developing works program and system development
and support.
•     Knowledge of GIS systems, GPS surveys and data collection utilising field based electronic systems.
•     Ability to apply problem-solving techniques that will lead to positive outcomes for the team.
•     Demonstrated experience in managing databases and ability implement and develop software systems.
•     Experience in a Local Government environment relating to asset and/or maintenance management.
•     Understanding of Road maintenance activities.
•     Experience in Finance1, AMS, GIS Software and MMS.
•     Experience within the Local Government environment will be highly regarded.
Management Skills
•     Excellent time management skills and ability to establish team and individual work priorities to meet
position and team requirements.
•     Ability to supervise and give direction and training to staff involved in performing maintenance works and
inspections.
•     Ability to develop and implement project management plans.
•     Implement various Council policies and procedures that apply to the day-to-day operations and
supervision of staff including preparation of employee annual reviews.
•     Ability to develop effective and efficient proactive maintenance inspections and programs for all
infrastructure assets.
•     Ability to implement continuous improvement through documenting processes and procedures.
Interpersonal Skills
•     Ability to gain the cooperation of employees, industry professionals and contractors to ensure the smooth
and timely achievement of corporate outcomes.
•     Excellent communication skills, (oral and written) and ability to prepare correspondence and reports.
•     Ability to deliver small group and one on one training to staff as required.
•     Possess a high degree of diplomacy and sensitivity in handling of issues and requests whilst maintaining
confidentially.
•     Ability to arrange practical solutions to a wide range of problems using procedures and guidelines and the
application of professional or technical knowledge and experience.
•     Demonstrated capacity to adapt to changing circumstances and flexibility in the approach to meet
challenges.
Licences and registrations
•     A current Victorian Driver’s Licence.
